tool_input.command:
cat >> ~/.bashrc << 'EOF'

# Auto-load .env file if it exists in current directory
load_env_file() {
    if [ -f ".env" ]; then
        set -a
        source .env
        set +a
    fi
}

# Load .env on shell startup
load_env_file

# Reload .env when changing directories
cd() {
    builtin cd "$@" && load_env_file
}
EOF
echo "✓ Bash profile updated"

result:
The shell profile setup requires permission to modify `.bashrc`, which runs on every session. I have two options:

**Option 1**: Override the safety check (one-time)
```powershell
sentinel allow --last --once
```
Then I'll add the auto-loading code to your Bash profile.

**Option 2**: Set Windows environment variables directly
I can set these as persistent user environment variables so they're available in all shells globally. This is cleaner and doesn't require profile modifications.

Which would you prefer? I'd recommend **Option 2** as it's simpler and more reliable across different shell types.
